answer: Anchor each identity to one basalt outpost: at random moments, several distant beacons send it a fresh challenge at once, and it must answer all of them within a latency bound no signal can beat from a single place. A nebula of clones run from one machine therefore fails the simultaneous replies, because light itself cannot carry one operator's answers to every beacon in time. Only a genuinely separate haven, with its own machine, link, and location, passes, so each clone needs a full new outpost while payout per identity stays flat.
